 Print this Article 
 View Comments Celtics center Neemias Queta (88) had a stronger night Friday against the Bulls, with 13 points, 6 rebounds, and just 1 foul in 20 minutes of play in the 125-111 NBA Cup win over Chicago at TD Garden. Barry Chin/Globe Staff After Jayson Tatum’s overtime buzzer-beater helped the Celtics escape with a 125-124 win over the Nets on Tuesday night, coach Joe Mazzulla quipped that Tatum should thank center Neemias Queta for making it possible. 
 There was more than a dash of sarcasm. After Tatum missed a free throw with the Celtics leading by 4 points with four seconds left in the fourth quarter, Queta inexplicably fouled Nets star Julius Randle , igniting a near-impossible chain of events that helped Brooklyn force the extra session. 
 Randle made his first free throw before intentionally missing the second. Mitchell Robinson , a poor free throw shooter, grabbed the rebound, was fouled and missed both free throws before Nets rookie Mikel Brown Jr. tied the score with a last-second 3-pointer. 
 “You prevent yourself from being in that position by not fouling 94 feet from the basket, so you don’t have to be in that situation,” Mazzulla said Tuesday. 
 Get Court Sense Keep up with everything Celtics with news, commentary, and analysis from the Globe's all-star team. Arrives twice weekly. Enter Email Sign Up Queta has dealt with foul trouble often during his Celtics tenure. He fouled out of Tuesday’s game in just 16 minutes. He found some redemption in Boston’s romp over the Bulls on Friday night , when he had 13 points, 6 rebounds, and just 1 foul in 20 minutes. 
 Related : Sunday Basketball Notes: Plethora of early-season injuries across the NBA landscape traces to new method of preserving players Afterward, he acknowledged that he must be better than he was Tuesday, particularly during that critical sequence at the end of the fourth quarter. 
 “I think it’s just being solid and sound,” Queta said. “Those things can’t happen. At the end of the day, I think the team needs me out there on the court more than on the bench. So, I think just being able to understand the impact I bring on the court and be smart in those moments.” 
 Celtics guard Payton Pritchard is hoping the Celtics can advance to the final four of the NBA Cup, thinking it'll help them later in the playoffs. Charles Krupa/AP Photo/Charles Krupa Celtics eye first real Cup run
 Aside from the glaring green floor that was used for Friday’s game, there were no real indications that it was an NBA Cup group-play matchup. Now entering its fourth year, the in-season tournament has yet to generate noticeable enthusiasm from fans. 
 But the Celtics, who have never advanced past the quarterfinals of the event, say they are motivated to make a longer run this season. 
 “People definitely want to win,” guard Payton Pritchard said. “Quite a bit of money on the table. Like, I definitely want to win. Even if it wasn’t the money, I’d still want to win. 
 “But playing in that environment and trying to be in those final four teams and playing and having that championship-mode again, I think it tests you and gets you ready for the playoffs. You see the Spurs and Knicks I think were in the Finals last year. I think it’s a good test and it can help you build for the future.” 
 Related : Opposing teams continue to leave Celtic Jordan Walsh wide open. He intends to make them pay. Players from the winning team will receive about $530,000 apiece. This season, the championship game will be held at Butler University’s Hinkle Fieldhouse on Dec. 11. 
 Celtics coach Joe Mazzulla was happy to put his clipboard down for a bit so he could see catch his stepson playing football for Xaverian Friday night. Barry Chin/Globe Staff Taking time for family
 Mazzulla usually conducts a press conference one hour, 45 minutes before each home game. But on Friday night, Mazzulla was replaced by assistant coach Tony Dobbins so he could attend the Senior Night football game of his stepson, Michael Harden Jr. , a Xaverian High linebacker who has committed to Boston College. 
 “It was cool. It was great,” Mazzulla said. “I appreciate my family. Just, obviously the job we have, unfortunately, the world revolves around me, and my family always has to do [expletive] for me all the time. And it was good to kind of put my stuff aside and just be a part of someone else’s story, and being there with his dad and family there, and it’s cool. 
 “Like, as a coach, you’re trying to have an impact, and then you see a group of coaches that we have at Xaverian, and they impacted my kid’s life the last four years, and it was good to say thanks to another coach, and it was good to see him compete.” 
 Xaverian defeated Malden Catholic, 27-14 .
